C-NATIVE-DOCX-RTF-EXPORT.Name: Native DOCX export without pandoc, plus export entries in the tab context menu: File menu and tab menu gain "Export to Word…" backed by a lazy renderer-side docx/html conversion of the styled export HTML, in every build including App Store; RTF deferred
C-NATIVE-DOCX-RTF-EXPORT.ApprovalBasis: Owner approved with explicit "ок" on 2026-10-23 (evening) over the revised spec — renderer-side docx/html architecture per the four-way bake-off, four fresh review passes green-after-fixes (Review 2), the modal-less owner decision folded in (Review 3), RTF out of v1, and the tab-context-menu export group merged as R-2 — authorizing plan creation under the standing four-corner review protocol.
C-NATIVE-DOCX-RTF-EXPORT.Summary: Mark can hand a document to a non-developer only as HTML/PDF today: DOCX exists solely through the external-pandoc bridge (M-015), which no user-facing menu item invokes anymore, and the App Store build reports pandoc unavailable by design; export commands also live only in the native File menu, a full menu-bar trip away from the tab the user is looking at. This change adds "Export to Word…" to the File menu and a fourth export group to the tab context menu (Export to PDF… / Export to HTML… / Export to Word…, gated like Copy path), backed by a renderer-only conversion: the same styled export HTML the HTML export already builds (with the M-065 local-image embed pass), pele/figure blocks pre-rasterized to PNG, then a lazy dynamic import of docx + docx/html converts it to a real Word document — native OMML equations from KaTeX's MathML, real Word footnotes, native task checkboxes — and the bytes are written through the existing mt_fs_write_binary. No new Rust writer, no new commands, no print surface: the path is structurally immune to the 2026-10-23 export-crash class and ships in the sandboxed MAS build unchanged. The engine choice is evidence-backed by the 2026-10-23 four-way bake-off (research/2026-10-23-docx-bakeoff + survey rounds 1-3), where the docx/html arm won or tied every contested construct and lazy-loads at ~237 KB gzip. RTF is out of v1: the same survey found no living ready-made RTF writer in any of our ecosystems, and the owner accepted deferral. The pandoc bridge stays untouched as a backend capability for exotic targets.

Problem.Description: Three facts define the gap. (1) There is no user-facing DOCX export anywhere: m009_menu.rs offers only file.export-file-pdf (line 567) and file.export-file-html (line 574); the renderer's only pandoc touchpoint is the status probe (src/renderer/src/ipc/runtime/integrations.ts:57, mt::pandoc::status), and mt_pandoc_status (src-tauri/src/m015_pandoc.rs:32) hard-returns available=false under the app-store feature — so a manager-facing "send me the spec as Word" moment has no Mark answer, on any build. (2) Export is reachable only from the native File menu, while the tab context menu (src/renderer/src/contextMenu/tabs/index.js: Close block, mode block, file block gated by !!pathname with Copy path) sits exactly where the user's pointer already is — a right-click "save this file as PDF/HTML/Word" is one door away and missing. (3) Typora exports DOCX out of the box and Obsidian's only DOCX route is a community pandoc plugin that their sandboxed and mobile builds cannot run either — a built-in converter puts Mark ahead on this axis (first-ever DOCX in the MAS build) while fitting the footprint story: no bundled pandoc, no binary growth, one lazy renderer chunk. Owner request 2026-10-23 (translated from Russian): "why is DOCX/RTF export hard without pandoc, and whether it is time to replace it the way bundled mermaid was replaced by pele", followed same day by "plan the spec together with extending the file menu and the header buttons for saving to different types — merge that feature in". The pele analogy holds: drop the general-purpose tool, ship a small specialized converter for exactly our format.

Goals.R-1: File → Export gains "Export to Word…" (menu id file.export-file-docx, command exportDocx, beside file.export-file-pdf / file.export-file-html, m009_menu.rs ~567). It runs in every build flavor, including app-store; not cfg-gated. Owner decision 2026-10-23: the export is MODAL-LESS from v1 — no settings dialog ever mounts for docx (pinned in e2e). One click: menu item (or tab-menu item) → native save dialog (plugin-dialog save, .docx filter, default name filename.md → filename.docx, untitled tab → derived title or "export" + .docx, mirroring the EXPORT defaultName logic in editor.js) → silent binary write. Page geometry comes from the remembered last-used export options — the same localStorage-backed options the ⌘P print path already reads (editor.js START_BLOCK_LAST_PRINT_OPTIONS, key mark-last-print-options; defaults A4 portrait, margins 20/15/20/15 mm per DEFAULT_PRINT_OPTIONS) — the in-product no-dialog precedent this flow copies. Success shows the existing success toast (exportSuccessTitle/Message, the C-56 pictures precedent) AND passes an actions descriptor — a quiet "Export settings" action with source 'export' — that today's legacy notify() silently ignores (extra properties drop; intentional temporary degradation) and that renders automatically once C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM lands (cross-change corner recorded in that bundle's design context; its target is the export-settings surface of the day: the existing exportSettings modal until the Export settings section exists, the section after). Cancel writes nothing and shows no notice; failure surfaces through the existing editor.export.failed error-notice pattern.
Goals.R-2: The tab context menu (contextMenu/tabs/index.js) gains a fourth group at the end, after the file block, gated by !!pathname exactly like Copy path: flat items "Export to PDF…", "Export to HTML…" and "Export to Word…" — labels byte-identical to the File menu items (one action, one name, two doors), flat not a submenu (discoverability mandate). Untitled tabs: all three disabled, same as Copy path. Preview/locked tabs: enabled, export is read-only with respect to the document. Clicking an export item on a background tab first activates that tab, then runs the identical existing flow, so the export always captures that tab's current buffer (unsaved edits included), same as the File menu. PDF/HTML items reuse the existing handlers end-to-end; the only new behavior in this group is the Word item from R-1.
Goals.R-3: The conversion pipeline is renderer-only and reuses existing machines: (a) build the styled export HTML exactly as the styledHtml branch does today — editor.value.exportStyledHTML (which re-renders through muya's own marked fork with the muya options: footnote, superSubScript, Prism highlight, KaTeX math renderer — the editor's own grammar, not a third-party parser); (b) run the existing M-065 embedLocalImages pass (src/renderer/src/util/exportImages.js, signature (rawHtml, documentDir) → {html, embedded, total, skipped}: local images to data-URLs, EMBED_CAP_BYTES 8 MiB, dedup, remote images never fetched); (c) pre-pass data-only fixes on the produced HTML: strip the pre.front-matter block (muya's renderer emits front matter as a pre block, renderer.js:13 — authoring metadata is not export body, the morning draft's stance kept deliberately) and replace exportable figure blocks (pele and the other C-56 roles resolved by diagramExport) with rasterized 2x PNG img data-URLs in document order; (d) lazy dynamic-import docx + docx/html on first use, convert with htmlToContent mapping our markup to named Word styles via styleMap/stylesheet options, wrap in a Document whose sectPr carries the remembered export options (pageSize / orientation / margins, same source as PDF), Packer.toBlob; (e) write the bytes through the same binary write facade the C-56 picture export uses (window.fileUtils.writeFile(path, bytes, 'binary'); backend mt_fs_write_binary, m013b fs.rs:370, with m010 sandbox path validation and C-24 write grants — the save-dialog path is the sandbox-safe target, the C-56 corner-7 precedent), via a 'docx' branch of the store EXPORT action mirroring the html branch's defaultName and dialog logic. No new Tauri command, no new capability, no new permission, no webview print call.
Goals.R-4: v1 construct coverage comes from muya's own export HTML (its marked fork re-render — the same grammar the editor itself uses, so no third-party markdown dialect enters the path): headings map to Word Heading 1-6 named styles; bold / italic / strikethrough / inline code / hyperlinks render as native runs and real w:hyperlink relationships; nested lists map to Word list levels; task-list checkboxes become native Word checkboxes (w14) with their checked state; tables become real tables with per-column alignment; fenced code blocks render monospace (Prism token spans in the source HTML degrade gracefully — token-level color in Word is a per-construct checklist verdict, not a promise); blockquotes render as quote-styled paragraphs; block and inline math become native OMML equations — the chain is KaTeX (which emits its MathML twin in the default output; all muya call sites pass no output option) → the export sanitizer, whose mathMl profile this change flips from false to true (T-002 discovery: EXPORT_DOMPURIFY_CONFIG stripped the twin, leaving an empty katex-mathml span; the flip restores it for the DOCX pipeline and for screen-reader parity with the live editor) → docx/html converts the MathML to Word equations. T-003 discovery (2026-10-24): muya's export grammar renders $$…$$ display blocks — standalone and inside list items — as literal text (a pre-existing gap today's HTML export shares; recorded as its own backlog item); inline $…$ spans convert to native equations now, display math joins automatically once the muya export-grammar fix lands, with zero pipeline changes — the input simply starts carrying MathML. Each of these was verified against real output in the 2026-10-23 bake-off (equations contain real m:f / m:nary / m:rad structures; footnotes.xml carries the definitions; checkbox states carry 0/1; hyperlinks resolve in document.xml.rels).
Goals.R-5: Footnotes (enabled by default in Mark — preferences.js sets footnote: true against muya's false default): muya's export HTML carries its own footnote shape (a.footnote-ref[role=doc-noteref] > sup references plus a section.footnotes[role=doc-endnotes] with hr + ordered list of li#fn…[role=doc-endnote] items and footnote-back links), which differs from the remark-rehype shape (data-footnote-ref / data-footnotes) the bake-off verified docx/html converts to real Word footnotes. The pre-pass therefore adapts the markup data-only to the recognized shape (attribute and structure reshaping on our own HTML; no muya change); a unit test pins muya's actual export-HTML footnote shape and asserts footnotes.xml in the output, so the adaptation is asserted, not assumed.
Goals.R-6: Honest degradations, recorded per-construct in the fidelity checklist rather than silently broken: remote http(s) images are never fetched (offline-deterministic, and the renderer CSP connect-src 'self' ipc: forbids external fetches by design) — they degrade to alt text plus the URL and count toward the M-065 skipped-images notice ("k of n images embedded"); any construct the importer maps poorly on real documents degrades visibly in the output and gets a checklist verdict; export never fails because of an image.
Goals.R-7: Footprint and dependency duties: docx ^9.14.0 is added as an npm dependency and the lockfile pins the exact version (npm ci in CI — the caret range never floats into a build); the docx + docx/html code loads only through the lazy dynamic import (no static import anywhere in the startup graph; the lazy chunk stays within a 300 KB gzip budget — 237 KB measured in the bake-off harness); NOTICES-node.md is regenerated to carry the docx MIT notice (existing gate), README Acknowledgements gains a docx line, the release notes of the shipping version mention the engine, and the published bake-off report (dolanmiu/docx discussion #3827) gets a follow-up comment when the release is out.
Goals.R-8: The fidelity matrix and a manual visual checklist (Word, Pages, LibreOffice; EN + RU fixtures) ship in docs/ with the change, including the bake-off-pinned expectations: a display formula inside a numbered list does not consume a list number (renders 1, 2 — the markdown-parser alternatives render 1, 2 (formula), 3), the front-matter block is absent from the body (stripped by the R-3c pre-pass; without the strip muya's own pre.front-matter would land as a code block), and code-block token colors get an explicit per-construct verdict.

Constraints.Item: No webview print container, no native print API, no Objective-C message anywhere in the new path: handleExport's 'docx' branch never calls printer.renderMarkdown, never invokes mt_export_pdf / mt_print_webview, and sends no native messages at all — it is structurally immune to the 2026-10-23 export-crash class (an invalid NSPrintInfo selector raising NSInvalidArgumentException through any Rust landing pad). Regression-pinned in e2e.

Implementation lands after the P1 print-crash fix (the printSettings dictionary-key patch in m052_print.rs plus its selector-audit test, queued as 2.8.1) merges to main: export-surface trust must be restored before a new export format and a second export entry point ship. This change does not edit m052_print.rs, safe_log.rs, mt_paths.rs or any release workflow (owned by the concurrent crash-fix session).

No new Tauri commands, capabilities or plugin permissions: the save dialog is the existing plugin-dialog save; the write rides the existing mt_fs_write_binary; the only Rust-side edit is the m009_menu.rs menu-item registration.

No network requests at export time (renderer CSP already forbids external connect-src; the requirement is stated so no relaxation is ever proposed); remote images stay URLs in the notice accounting, same rule as M-065.

The DOCX pipeline must consume the same styled-HTML builder the HTML export uses — no second HTML generator to keep true. If C-SELF-CONTAINED-HTML-EXPORT refactors exportImages.js or the styledHtml builder, this change follows the moved util; the shared dependency is named, not forked. Amendment (T-002 discovery, 2026-10-24): the bundle's only muya change is the EXPORT_DOMPURIFY_CONFIG mathMl profile flip (one word, src/muya/lib/config/index.js) that keeps KaTeX's inert MathML twin in exported HTML; the constraint against generator changes stands for everything else.
docx is imported only through the lazy dynamic-import path; a CI-checked script asserts the entry chunk contains no docx code and the docx dynamic chunk stays ≤ 300 KB gzip.

RTF is out of scope for this bundle: the 2026-10-23 survey (mark-private research doc, RTF section) found no living ready-made writer in npm, Rust or the native endpoint's fidelity class worth depending on; revisit only on real field demand, with the hand-rolled Rust writer as Plan A and the native macOS NSAttributedString endpoint as Plan B (both documented in the survey).

Hostile document text can never forge document structure: the converter consumes DOM-parsed HTML through htmlToContent (not string concatenation into XML), and the docx library's serialization layer performs the XML escaping; a hostile-text fixture (raw braces, control bytes, fake footnote markup, fake style attributes) round-trips into a valid .docx whose text nodes equal the source text, pinned in the unit matrix.

Tab-menu labels stay byte-identical to File-menu labels; every new label and notice lands as native copy in all ten static/locales/*.json; menu labels and notices are written by the change, not translated mechanically.

Every governed edit ships MODULE_CONTRACT / MODULE_MAP / CHANGE_SUMMARY; grace lint --path . --assertions current = 0; graph (DF-007 export flow branch, M-066 renderer converter, tab-menu module note) and verification documents update in the same change.

NonGoals.NonGoal: RTF export in this bundle (deferred with Plan A/Plan B documented in the survey; the change id keeps its historical name for stability).
Import of DOCX/RTF; export to EPUB/LaTeX/OpenOffice (the pandoc bridge keeps serving those who need it).
Generated table of contents in the output (the Word TOC field that prompts "update fields" on open); comments / tracked-changes interop (C-26 territory).

Any pre-export settings dialog or per-format options UI for Word (modal-less by owner decision 2026-10-23; geometry silently follows the remembered print/export options; the per-export override returns later through the notification's quiet "Export settings" action once C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM lands, and the Export settings section itself is the separate backlog rework).
A second HTML pipeline, an HTML sanitizer rewrite, or changes to muya's export-HTML generator beyond what R-5's data-only pre-pass adaptation needs.
Figure roles beyond the C-56 exportable set — they follow C-56's own follow-up, not this bundle.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: vitest unit matrix green on the pre-pass and the conversion. Pre-pass: image embed counts and skip accounting reuse the M-065 semantics (local ≤ 8 MiB embedded, cap-exceeded and failed reads skipped, remote skipped with URL preserved); figure replacement is by document order and produces valid PNG data-URLs; muya's real export-HTML footnote shape is pinned. Conversion (EN + RU fixtures): the unzipped output's word/document.xml contains Heading1..Heading6 pStyles, a w:tbl whose cells carry per-column jc, a w:hyperlink resolving in document.xml.rels, monospace code runs, w14:checkbox elements with the fixture's checked states, and m:oMath equations whose content includes a fraction and an n-ary structure; word/footnotes.xml carries the RU footnote text with its bold run; no front-matter text appears anywhere (the pre-pass strips muya's pre.front-matter block — pinned on muya's real export output); word/document.xml sectPr matches the remembered page geometry; the display formula inside the numbered list does not consume a list number (numbering walk renders 1, 2).

Hostile-text fixture round-trip: a document containing raw braces, control bytes, fake footnote markup and fake style attributes exports to a valid .docx whose concatenated text nodes equal the source text; nothing from the fixture appears as document structure.

e2e (tauri-shim): Export to Word… opens the save dialog with a .docx default name and writes the file through mt_fs_write_binary; NO export-settings component ever mounts on the docx path (pinned); cancel invokes the write zero times, writes nothing, shows no notice. Tab context menu: the fourth group shows the three export items; gated by pathname (untitled tabs disabled); clicking Export on a background tab activates it and exports that tab's buffer; PDF/HTML items run the existing flows unchanged. The pdf, print and styledHtml branches behave byte-for-byte as before (print-export.spec.ts and export-html-images.spec.ts stay green untouched); the docx branch never invokes mt_export_pdf / mt_print_webview (pinned).

Notification contract: the success path calls the existing toast with the exportSuccessTitle/Message keys AND passes the actions descriptor (quiet "Export settings", source 'export'); a unit test pins the call shape — the legacy wrapper ignores the extra fields today, and the same call renders the action automatically under C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM (corner recorded in that bundle's design context, export-settings-action-2026-10-23).
Lazy-chunk guard: the CI script builds the renderer and asserts no docx code in the entry chunk and the docx dynamic chunk ≤ 300 KB gzip; the build stays green on npm test.

Dependency and attribution duties: package.json pins docx ^9.14.0; NOTICES-node.md carries the docx MIT entry and its gate passes; README Acknowledgements gains the docx line; the follow-up comment to dolanmiu/docx discussion #3827 is drafted in the change's checklist (sent at release time, per the approval-before-outward-sends rule).

Localization: the File-menu label, the three tab-menu labels (shared wording with the File-menu items), the images-embedded notice and the quiet "Export settings" action label (shipped now so the balloon needs no new keys later) present as native copy in all ten locales; placeholders verified.

Manual acceptance checklist passes: the EN and RU fidelity fixtures export and open without warnings in Word, Pages and LibreOffice; page geometry (landscape-A4 fixture with custom margins) matches the remembered options; the math-in-list and front-matter expectations from R-8 hold visually; export of the 100 KB stress fixture completes in under 3 seconds on the dev machine; checklist committed under docs/ with per-construct verdicts.

npm test green; grace lint --path . --assertions current = 0; .grace/graph/flows.xml DF-007 gains the docx branch, .grace/graph/features.xml gains the M-066 renderer-converter entry and the tab-menu group note, .grace/verification/features.xml gains the export-office entries.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npx playwright test tests/e2e/export-office.spec.ts tests/e2e/print-export.spec.ts tests/e2e/export-html-images.spec.ts --project=chromium
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Unzipped-output structural assertions (styles, rels, footnotes.xml, OMML content, checkbox states, numbering walk) on EN+RU fixtures including the hostile-text round-trip; pre-pass unit matrix reusing the M-065 corner semantics (cap, failure, remote, dedup, document-order figures); e2e wiring through the shim with cancel and regression pins (pdf/print/styledHtml untouched, no print-container invocation); lazy-chunk build guard (entry chunk clean, docx chunk ≤ 300 KB gzip); manual Word/Pages/LibreOffice checklist with per-construct verdicts and the 3-second budget; NOTICES gate and README line present.

Assumptions.Assumption: docx 9.14.0's htmlToContent behaves on real documents as measured in the 2026-10-23 bake-off (mark-private research/2026-10-23-docx-bakeoff/ + survey Round 3 + post-audit): KaTeX MathML converts to native OMML with real structure, markdown-style footnotes to real Word footnotes, checkbox inputs to w14 checkboxes, and a formula inside a list item stays un-numbered. The bake-off fixture was synthetic; the plan re-runs the same assertions on muya-rendered export HTML at implementation start, and the harness artifacts are preserved for replication. Fallback if the importer stumbles on production CSS: markdown-docx (the bake-off's close second; needs our front-matter strip and its math-in-list numbering shape) with the same pre-pass and write machinery — the pipeline's steps (a)-(c) and (e) are engine-agnostic by design.

muya's export-HTML footnote markup is either recognized by docx/html directly or adaptably by the data-only pre-pass (R-5); the unit test on muya's real output decides the branch, and neither branch changes muya.

The lazy chunk measured 237 KB gzip in the bake-off's esbuild browser harness; Vite chunking may differ slightly, hence the 300 KB in-app budget with the CI guard. No katex duplication exists in this arm (docx has no katex dependency — math input is our existing rendered HTML).

Word, Pages and LibreOffice render the output constructs; Pages' OMML import has mixed community reports, so the manual checklist treats Pages as a recorded verdict, not a gate-blocking requirement (Word is the primary target).

The P1 print-crash fix (printSettings dictionary-key patch, 2.8.1) merges to main before implementation starts; M-065's exportImages.js and the styledHtml builder remain importable at their current homes or announce their moves (C-SELF-CONTAINED-HTML-EXPORT owns them; additive coordination, both changes active in the same window).
